title: Fan-out amplification — N×K load, connection pools, rate limits, timeouts, circuit breakers

s1_definition.profdef: **Fan-out amplification**: if your service receives N requests/second and each fans out to K downstream calls via `CompletableFuture.allOf()`, the downstream sees N×K requests/second. 1000 req/s × 3 downstream calls = 3000 downstream req/s. This can OVERWHELM downstream services, databases, and connection pools. Parallelizing with CF without proper safeguards creates a DDoS-like effect on your own infrastructure. **Required safeguards**: (1) **Connection pool sizing**: HikariCP maxPoolSize must handle N×K concurrent connections. (2) **Rate limiting**: limit outbound calls per second (Resilience4j RateLimiter). (3) **Timeouts**: every call has a deadline (orTimeout). (4) **Circuit breaker**: if downstream fails, stop sending requests (Resilience4j CircuitBreaker). (5) **Bulkhead**: bounded thread pool per downstream.
s1_definition.analogy: Your bank branch (service) serves 1000 customers/hour. Each customer needs 3 checks: credit bureau, property valuation, income verification. Your branch sends 3000 calls/hour to these agencies. If the credit bureau can only handle 500/hour → OVERWHELMED → rejects requests → YOUR customers fail. You just DDoS'd your own partner! Fix: rate limit (max 500/hour to bureau), circuit breaker (if bureau down → stop calling for 60s), timeout (5s max per call), connection pool (sized for max concurrent).
s1_definition.oneliner: N requests × K fan-out = N×K downstream load. Parallelism without safeguards = self-inflicted DDoS. Must: size connection pools, rate limit, timeout, circuit break per downstream.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The loan approval service received 1000 req/s, each fanning out to 3 APIs.** 3000 downstream calls/s. Credit bureau limit: 500/s → rejected 2500/s → 83% loan approvals failed! HikariCP: 20 connections, 1000 concurrent queries → connection timeout → cascade failure. Fix: (1) Rate limiter: 500/s to bureau. (2) Circuit breaker: opens at 50% failure → fast-fail for 60s. (3) Timeout: 5s per call. (4) Bulkhead: 20-thread pool per downstream. (5) HikariCP: 100 connections. Result: graceful degradation under load, zero cascade failures.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** Service receives 1000 req/s. Each fans out to 3 CF calls. Downstream sees 3000 req/s.

**Step 2 (no safeguards).** Credit bureau capacity: 500/s → rejects 2500/s → 83% failure rate. HikariCP: 20 connections for 1000 concurrent → timeout. Thread pool: 50 threads for 1000 concurrent → queue overflow.

**Step 3 (with safeguards).** Semaphore/rate limiter: max 500/s to bureau. Circuit breaker: opens at 50% failure → fast-fail. Timeout: 5s per call → thread freed. Bulkhead: 20-thread pool per downstream → max 20 concurrent.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ FAN-OUT AMPLIFICATION ═══

  Incoming: 1000 req/s
  Each request: allOf(creditBureau, propertyAPI, incomeVerify)
  Downstream: 1000 × 3 = 3000 calls/s!

  Credit bureau capacity: 500/s → OVERWHELMED! 2500 rejected!

  ═══ SAFEGUARDS ═══

  Rate limiter:    max 500/s to bureau → excess waits/rejected
  Circuit breaker: 50% failure → OPEN → fast-fail (10ms) for 60s
  Timeout:         5s per call → thread freed, not stuck 300s
  Bulkhead:        20-thread pool → max 20 concurrent to bureau
  Connection pool: HikariCP 100 → supports concurrent queries
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — Fan-Out Safeguard Stack ═══

  Per downstream dependency:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  1. Bulkhead (ThreadPoolExecutor)     │  limits concurrent calls
  │     core:10, max:20, queue:100       │
  │                                        │
  │  2. Circuit Breaker (Resilience4j)    │  stops calls when failing
  │     failureRate:50%, openDuration:60s │
  │                                        │
  │  3. Rate Limiter (Resilience4j)       │  limits calls/sec
  │     limit:500/sec, timeout:100ms     │
  │                                        │
  │  4. Timeout (orTimeout)               │  prevents thread hang
  │     deadline: 5 seconds               │
  │                                        │
  │  5. Connection Pool (HikariCP)        │  limits DB connections
  │     maxPoolSize: 100                  │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  Without safeguards:
  1000 req/s × 3 fan-out = 3000/s → overwhelm → cascade failure!

  With safeguards:
  Each downstream: max 500/s, 20 concurrent, 5s timeout, circuit break
  Graceful degradation, zero cascade!
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Fan-out amplification: N incoming requests × K downstream calls per request = N×K downstream load. 1000 req/s × 3 calls = 3000 downstream req/s. Parallelizing with CompletableFuture without safeguards is a self-inflicted DDoS on your own dependencies. Five required safeguards per downstream: bulkhead (bounded thread pool limits concurrent calls), rate limiter (caps calls/second), timeout (orTimeout prevents thread hang), circuit breaker (stops calling when failing — fast-fail for 60s), and connection pool sizing (HikariCP maxPoolSize handles concurrent connections).

Without safeguards: credit bureau at 500/s capacity receives 3000/s → rejects 83% → loan service cascade failure. With safeguards: rate limited to 500/s, circuit breaks at 50% failure, excess requests degrade gracefully with cached scores. In banking: every downstream dependency needs its own safeguard stack. The combination of bulkhead + circuit breaker + rate limiter + timeout is called the "resilience stack" — standard in microservices (Resilience4j, Istio service mesh).

---

keyPoints: One request triggers N calls, each triggers K more
Mitigation: pools, rate limits, timeouts, circuit breakers
